It can be. Canada uses a point system to determine eligibility. The best process is to get a job here, get a work visa, find a place to live, then move. Once here you can apply for permanent residence. After you've been in country for four years as a permanent resident you can apply for citizenship. That was the route I took.

All in, it will cost you a few thousand dollars for all the applications fees, paperwork, etc. More if you hire a company to help. The process can be confusing so some people hire a 3rd party for assistance. What I didn't know when I did this is the local MP (Member of Parliament) constituency office can often help navigate the process. Some MP offices are better than others so you can research this before you move and find a district with an MP who can help you - then move in that area. Since you'll be working and paying Canadian taxes, you might as well take advantage of your tax dollar at work.

A few people I know are fine with permanent residence, but you have to keep renewing your card - which costs money and the paperwork sucks. It isn't that much more work to apply for citizenship.
